content.text: No audit right binding our side exists anywhere in the document. Submitting a compliant finding without a redline.

input.quote: Upon reasonable request not more than once during any calendar year, and with reasonable notice, the Servicer will give the Issuer, the Depositor, the Parent Support Provider, the Administrator, the Owner Trustee and the Indenture Trustee (or their representatives) access to the records and documents to conduct a review of the Servicer's performance under this Agreement.
input.rationale: The AUDIT rule constrains audit/inspection rights that bind us. Searching the full document for audit, inspection, examination, verification, records and access surfaced only two review clauses, and both run in our favour rather than against us. Section 3.6 (p0131) obliges the Servicer (Cellco, the counterparty) to give the Issuer, Depositor, Administrator, Owner Trustee and Indenture Trustee access to its records to review the Servicer's performance, and Section 3.9(e) (p0146) obliges the Custodian (also Cellco) to give the Depositor, Issuer and Indenture Trustee access to the Receivable Files and receivables systems. The remaining hits are the same direction: p0437 requires the Servicer to deliver records to the Administrator and Issuer for Regulation AB compliance, and p0446-p0447 require the Servicer to grant the Asset Representations Reviewer access. Cellco has no reciprocal right to audit, inspect or access the Issuer's or Depositor's records or systems, so none of the walk-away triggers (unlimited or unannounced audits, remote access to our systems) is present and there is no counterparty audit right to which the frequency, notice and cost parameters could attach. Nothing here is adverse to us and no redline is warranted. Two observations noted but not flagged: the planner's question whether the policy qualifiers gut our access, i.e. that our review rights under Sections 3.6 and 3.9(e) are "subject to the Servicer's security, confidentiality and privacy policies and any regulatory, legal and data protection policies", concerns the strength of our own inspection rights and is outside this rule's checklist, which only limits audits against us; expanding our access would fall under a separate audit-rights-in-our-favour position. Likewise the requirement that access be exercised "by all parties at the same time" at the Servicer's offices is a constraint on our own right, not an obligation imposed on us.
